messages:
priya: heads-up: spike in NVMe temps + i/o errors in ap-south1 affecting gpu attach for batch jobs
omar: saw alerts. which hosts?
priya: ephemeral-scratch-03 pool. sample hosts: gnode-apse1-210..216. dmesg tail: 
priya: ```
[ 98765.123456] nvme1n1: I/O error, index 0x2f
[ 98765.234567] nvme1n1: media_error LBA 0x3a1b
[ 98765.345678] nvme1n1: critical temperature threshold exceeded: 76C
```
kevin: smartctl shows increasing reallocated sectors on gnode-214
kevin: Smart snippet: Reallocated_Sector_Ct Raw_Value=6, Temp=76
dina: timeline: started ~2026-03-22 23:05 UTC after overnight firmware wave; janitor scrub ops jumped concurrently
priya: hypothesis: FW changed TRIM/coalesce timing -> more small write flushes -> thermal + write amp
omar: immediate mitigation ideas?
kevin: 1) pause janitor scrub for this pool, 2) mark affected hosts as no-gpu-attach, 3) canary rollback of FW on one host
dina: pausing janitor is low-friction; we need to ensure backlog doesn't cause user-visible GC later
priya: agree. I'll reduce janitor cadence to 2x and add backlog monitor alert
omar: I'll start draining gnode-210..216 from gpu-service, will run drain -q on each; expect 8-12m
priya: also try toggling nvme_trim_aggressive=0 on a canary kernel to see temp effect
kevin: can we run fio read/write workload to reproduce? I'd rather reproduce on canary than risk rollback
kevin: fio cmd: fio --name=smallwrite --rw=randwrite --bs=4k --iodepth=16 --size=10G --numjobs=4
priya: good call. run on gnode-212 after drain completes
ods-bot: Action logged: created incident INC-APSE-NVME-03; responders: priya, omar, kevin, dina
priya: vendor already paged; asked for firmware changelog and whether trim timing was altered
dina: cost note: shifting launch traffic out of ap-south1 will add ~+$900/day in spot premiums and cross-region egress if sustained
omar: status: drain started on gnode-210; currently migrating pods, 3 remaining
kevin: canary kernel flag applied on gnode-212, running fio. initial temps: 73C -> after fio steady at 70C
priya: preliminary telemetry: canary shows 30% lower write amplification and fewer temp spikes
kevin: yara: no user-visible corruption reported. only kernel blocks and increased reassign counts
ods-bot: Update: INC-APSE-NVME-03 status=investigating
dina: follow-up ops plan: 1) pause janitor on pool 2) complete drain of 7 hosts 3) run canary fio + kernel toggle 4) vendor escalation for FW rollback/RMA policy
priya: I'm applying janitor cadence change now (60m -> 120m) and enabling backlog alert at 50%
omar: drained 7 hosts, attach failures dropped from ~11% -> 2% in 20m
kevin: vendor reply: they see TRIM scheduler change in release notes, paused further rollouts, investigating mitigations
dina: schedule postmortem for tomorrow 09:30 UTC. include telemetry, vendor diff, procurement follow-up for drive lifecycle risk
priya: adding dashboard tiles: nvme_temp_p95, nvme_reassign_rate, gpu_attach_fail_pct, janitor_ops/s
kevin: will keep canary under test for 6h before recommending kernel toggle fleetwide
ods-bot: Incident INC-APSE-NVME-03 updated: status=mitigated responders=[priya, omar, kevin, dina]
priya: thanks team. leaving thread for postmortem notes
omar: thanks all :thumbsup:
